Mrs. Gorham states that he is an Englishman who acquired wealth in mining, yet I think he will prove to be a Yankee. He undoubtedly possesses wealth, because he recently lavished Odette with jewels. The engagement ring she received is a cluster of diamonds of such great size that it resembles a bandage on Odette’s plump hand.”

A certain sharp resentment inevitably crept into Mrs. Sowerby’s voice. Although Nell had apparently not been sought after by a single suitor, whether wealthy or destitute, Odette Pullen—that unremarkable, dull worker—had managed to secure a proposal from a man of immense fortune. Furthermore, Mrs. Gorham Pullen boasted beyond endurance.
“What has been happening with Hugh Carrow at college?” Thirza inquired. “Upon seeing him when he returned home last week, he appeared so pale and thin that I barely recognized him.”

“During this past winter, his studies were very intense,” Nell remarked. “As you are aware, he earned High Honors in Classics along with the Cooper Prize. No one has won it in five years! Consequently, I believe he is quite exhausted. Every one of us is somewhat weary.”
“At least you possess a B.A., whereas Odette Pullen does not have one and never will,” Mrs. Sowerby remarked, expressing a sombre sense of gratification.

A couple of nights afterward, Nell walked down to visit Odette, although she was out of town in Port Marlow—“getting sewing done,” Mrs. Gorham proudly told Nell. “Of course an Brierley dressmaker wouldn’t do for Odette under the circumstances.”
“Regarding Odette, a particularly pleasant piece of news has reached my ears,” remarked Nell.

“Indeed, Odette has managed quite well, despite not holding a B.A.,” stated Mrs. Gorham, lightly tossing her head. “Mr. Inglis possesses millions, and Europe is where they will travel for their honeymoon. Upon returning, a true marble mansion in Winnipeg will be their residence. A single difficulty faces Odette—her culinary skills are great, yet her husband forbids her to prepare meals. His wealth is such that he employs others for cooking. Their household will include a cook, a pair of additional maids, a coachman, and a general handyman. However, what of your situation, Nell? Despite all your time at college, I receive no news regarding a marriage for you.”

“Oh,” Nell chuckled, “an old maid is what I am destined to be. Truly, no one seems to suit me.” Her remark carried a touch of malice. She purposefully intended to make Mrs. Pullen remember that should she end up an unwed woman, a lack of at least one opportunity to marry would not be the reason. Mrs. Gorham, however, retaliated without delay.

“Indeed, those overly selective young women usually wind up single, from what I see. And what is this news I am receiving regarding Hugh Carrow becoming betrothed to a Miss Calder? Wilfred Mott informs me that she possesses absolute beauty. Does truth lie in this?”
“I am unsure whether his engagement to Miss Calder is a fact,” Nell answered with Spartan calm, “yet her great beauty is undoubtedly real.”
“I formerly believed that a marriage would come about between you and Hugh,” Mrs. Gorham remarked. “If you are not cautious, Nell, every one of your suitors will slip away from you.”
Nell chose against prolonging her fight with Mrs. Gorham. It was impossible to engage in swordplay with an opponent who answered a rapier’s lunges using the stroke of a battle axe.
“Because Odette is out,” she stated, standing up in a proud manner, “I doubt I should remain any further today. I will return once she arrives back.”

“Please do,” Mrs. Gorham uttered with enthusiasm. “Odette lacks any pride whatsoever. Her intention is simply to mingle with her previous acquaintances precisely as she used to do. Seeing you will make her truly happy.”

At the end of May, the millionaire belonging to Odette came and whisked her away amidst grand magnificence. Discovering that Mr. Inglis was a full forty years old, as well as diminutive, slender, and somewhat graying, gave Mrs. Sowerby a malicious sense of satisfaction. You can be certain that Mrs. Sowerby refrained from holding back as she listed his defects.
“A pill like him will require all of his gold for gilding, that is a fact,” Mrs. Agatha stated with gravity.
“His appearance seems gentle and benevolent,” Nell stated faithfully, “and I have no doubt that Odette means everything to him.”
“Humph!” remarked Mrs. Agatha.

Cressy Lindsay was wedded during the following week, with Nell traveling to Harborough so she could serve as her bridesmaid. The bride, Cressy, appeared as a delicate, ethereal fairy, while the Rev. Ez beamed with such intense joy that no person considered his looks to be plain.

“Through the land of Evangeline, we’ll be taking a lovers’ saunter,” Cressy remarked, “and afterward, Tanner Street is where we will settle down. It is terrible, according to Mother—she believes Ez could find a church in a respectable location, at the very least. However, provided Ez is present, the Patterson slums' wilderness is going to blossom for me like the rose. Oh, Nell, my heart is aching with how happy I am.”

Nell continually felt joy when her friends were happy; nevertheless, being encircled on all sides by a joy that does not belong to oneself can feel somewhat lonely at times. Furthermore, things remained precisely identical once she returned to Brierley. On this occasion, Isolde was the one enveloped in the marvelous radiance that arrives for a woman as her first child is placed next to her. Nell observed the pale young mother with a particular reverence that had not previously been part of her emotions toward Isolde. Was it possible that this pallid woman, whose eyes held such ecstasy, was the small, rosy-cheeked Isolde with black curls whom she used to play with during bygone schooldays? It imparted to her a strange, abandoned sensation that she was somehow anchored solely to those former years, possessing no place in the present whatsoever.
“Isn’t he completely handsome?” asked Isolde with pride.

The small, chubby man bore a ridiculous resemblance to Gideon, possessing an identical roundness and redness. Though Nell was unable in good conscience to declare him handsome, she swore with complete honesty that he was charming, affectionate, and utterly lovely.

“Prior to his arrival, I desired a female child, enabling me to name her NELL,” Isolde stated. “However, now that young Gideon has arrived, I would not swap him for one million girls. It was simply impossible for him to be anything other than his individual cherished self.”
“‘Every little baby is the sweetest and the best,’” Mrs. Wace gaily quoted. “If little Nell had arrived, your feelings regarding her would have been identical.”

Mrs. Wace was on a visit to Brierley, which marked her initial return there after her departure. She remained just as lively, charming, and understanding as she had always been. Her former female companions had given her a joyous and enthusiastic welcome upon her return. Although the wife of the current minister was an admirable woman, she was not quite a like-minded soul.

“I am so eager for the time when he is big enough to speak,” Isolde sighed. “Hearing him call me ‘mother’ is my deepest desire. And oh, I am resolved that he will have a pleasant first recollection of me. My own earliest remembrance of my mother involves her striking me because of an act I had committed. I have no doubt that I merited the punishment, and my mother was invariably wonderful and holds a special place in my heart. Even so, I truly wish that my initial memory concerning her had been more agreeable.”

“My mother lives in only a single recollection of mine, which surpasses every other memory in sweetness,” Mrs. Wace stated. “Upon reaching five years of age, permission was granted for me to attend school on a single occasion alongside my two elder sisters. As the school day concluded, my sisters departed for home within separate companionships, as both assumed the other had me in their care. In reality, I had departed alongside a young girl who had been my playmate during recess. Together, we proceeded to her house located close to the school, where we commenced forming mud pies. An exceptionally wonderful time was being had by us at the moment my elder sister appeared, winded and enraged.

"“Naughty girl,” she exclaimed, seizing my unyielding hand and pulling me behind her. “Return home immediately. Oh, you will be punished! Mother is extremely angry. You are going to receive a thorough whipping.”

“I had not ever been beaten. My poor small heart was overwhelmed with dread and terror. Never in my existence had I been so unhappy as during that return journey. Being bad had not been my intention. Phemy Cameron had invited me to accompany her home, and I had been unaware that going was improper. Now, however, I was facing a whipping because of it. Upon our arrival home, my sister pulled me along into the kitchen, where mother was seated beside the fire as the twilight fell. My poor little legs shook to such a degree that standing was nearly impossible. And mother—mother simply gathered me into her arms, offering not a single word of scolding or severity, kissed me, and pressed me near to her heart. ‘I was so frightened you were lost, darling,’ she said tenderly. As she gazed down at me, I was able to see the love glowing in her eyes. She did not ever reprimand or criticize me for my actions—she merely instructed me that I must not ever depart again without seeking consent. She passed away shortly after that. That remains the sole recollection I possess of her. Isn’t it a beautiful one?”

As she journeyed toward her house, traveling by the Aspen Path and Reedmere, Nell experienced a isolation deeper than any she had known before. Many moons had passed since she last traveled that route. The night was a rich, dark purple. The atmosphere hung thick with the scent of blooms—an intensity that was nearly overwhelming. From this excessive sweetness, the sated senses shrank back as if from a brimming glass. The birches lining the track, once the magical saplings of former days, had matured into large trees. All things were altered. Nell believed she would feel relieved once summer ended and her employment resumed. It might be that her existence would not appear so void at that point.
“‘I have put the world to the test—it displays no longer The romantic hues it once displayed,’”
uttered Nell with a sigh—and she felt instantly greatly reassured by how romantic it was to think that all romance had been stripped from the world!

text: For the summer, the Irvings returned to Echo Cottage, where Nell enjoyed a delightful three-week stay during July. No change had come over Miss Rosalind; although Belinda the Fourth had become a quite mature young woman by this time, her affectionate devotion to Nell remained genuine.

chapter_title: Chapter XL A Book of Revelation
text: “Taking everything into account, Miss Harcourt, ma’am, I haven’t come across a single person in Boston who compares to you,” she declared openly.

chapter_title: Chapter XL A Book of Revelation
text: Cedric had nearly reached adulthood as well. Having reached the age of sixteen, he now sported short-cut brown hair instead of his former chestnut curls, and his enthusiasm for football had surpassed his interest in fairies. Even so, the connection that linked him to his former instructor remained intact. It is only kindred spirits that remain unaltered as time passes.

chapter_title: Chapter XL A Book of Revelation
text: It was a dreary, harsh, and rain-soaked July evening when Nell returned to Grey Shutters. The ocean was being battered by one of those violent summer storms that occasionally rush across the gulf. The initial drops of rain struck the windows just as Nell entered.

chapter_title: Chapter XL A Book of Revelation
text: “Did Cedric bring you back?” Thirza inquired. “You should have had him spend the night. The weather tonight is going to be rough.”

chapter_title: Chapter XL A Book of Revelation
text: “My belief is that he will arrive at Echo Cottage prior to the rain becoming particularly severe. In any case, returning this evening was his desire. Indeed, my stay was marvelous, though returning to you beloved people brings me joy. ‘East, west, hame’s best.’ Robin, is it the case that you have grown taller again recently?”

chapter_title: Chapter XL A Book of Revelation
text: “Since you departed, I have grown an entire inch,” Robin said with pride. “Now I am just as tall as Milty Gammon. Am I not happy. Being bigger is something he will have to cease boasting about. Tell me, Nell, were you aware that Hugh Carrow is passing away?” Looking at Robin, Nell remained completely still and quiet. Thirza believed she would swoon because her face had turned so pale.

chapter_title: Chapter XL A Book of Revelation
text: “Robin, keep quiet,” Mrs. Agatha uttered with anger. “Nell, stop making that face—stop making that face! Our intention was not to inform you with such suddenness.”

chapter_title: Chapter XL A Book of Revelation
text: “Is—it—true?” Nell questioned using a voice that did not belong to her.

chapter_title: Chapter XL A Book of Revelation
text: “Hugh is extremely sick,” Mrs. Sowerby stated solemnly. “Right after you departed for Echo Cottage, he came down with typhoid fever. Were you never told about it?”

chapter_title: Chapter XL A Book of Revelation
text: “No,” replied the unidentified voice.

chapter_title: Chapter XL A Book of Revelation
text: “From the beginning, it was an extremely severe situation. His health had been severely depleted, according to the physician. A professional nurse is present, and every possible measure has been taken. Do not wear that expression, Nell. As long as life remains, hope persists.”

chapter_title: Chapter XL A Book of Revelation
text: “Mr. Pettifer was present tonight and he stated that they possessed no expectation for him,” Robin repeated.

chapter_title: Chapter XL A Book of Revelation
text: Thirza, who appeared weary, aged, and exhausted, stood up and sternly escorted Robin out of the kitchen.

chapter_title: Chapter XL A Book of Revelation
text: “Oh, do not have that expression, dear,” Mrs. Agatha said, placing her gentle, aged arms around the pale girl. “I really have not surrendered hope, I truly have not. He has the advantage of the Carrow constitution, that is the thing.”

chapter_title: Chapter XL A Book of Revelation
text: Nell softly disengaged herself from Mrs. Sowerby’s embrace, navigated the kitchen without seeing, passed through the hall, and climbed the staircase to the bedroom that had been hers. Kneeling by its window, she gazed outside with eyes that saw nothing. Darkness hung heavily everywhere. Over the quivering fields, rain poured ceaselessly. The Haunted Woods echoed with the moaning of huge trees twisted by the storm, while the air vibrated with the deafening roar of waves breaking against the far-off coast. And Hugh was on the brink of death!

chapter_title: Chapter XL A Book of Revelation
text: Just as the Bible contains a book of Revelation, so does the life of every individual. As Nell maintained her agonizing watch throughout the hours of darkness and storm on that bitter night, she read her own. She loved Hugh—she had loved him always! That was clear to her now. She recognized that casting him from her life without agony was no more possible than severing her right hand and throwing it away would be. Yet this realization had arrived too late—too late for even the bitter comfort of standing beside him in his final moments. Had she not been so blind—so foolish—she would now possess the right to join him. Instead, he would pass from this life believing she did not care, never knowing that she loved him. Oh, the dark, empty years unfolding ahead of her! Living through them was impossible—she simply could not! Cowering by her window, she wished that she could die as well, a desire she had never felt before in her gay young life. Should Hugh depart from her without a single word, sign, or message, her life could not continue. Without him, nothing held any value. She was his, and he was hers. During this moment of ultimate agony, she harbored no doubt regarding that truth. He did not love Rowena Calder—he had never loved Rowena Calder. Oh, what a fool she was for failing to see the nature of the bond tying her to Hugh—for mistaking the flattered fancy she harbored for Cyril Lisle for true love. And now, as if it were a crime, her folly demanded payment.

chapter_title: Chapter XL A Book of Revelation
text: Prior to retiring for the night, Mrs. Sowerby and Thirza stole up to her doorway, silently exchanged uncertain nods at the quietness, and departed. Throughout the night the tempest continued furiously, yet it had exhausted itself by the time morning arrived. Nell observed a delicate, enchanted border of brightness along the edges of the night. Shortly thereafter, a glowing, ruby-like edge appeared upon the crests of the eastern hills. The clouds gathered into huge, gentle, pale heaps along the skyline as they moved off; the heavens shone with a silvery, azure light. A quietness descended upon the earth.

chapter_title: Chapter XL A Book of Revelation
text: Rising from her knees, Nell crept downstairs. As she stepped into the yard, the cool, fresh rain-wind blew against her pale face, soothing her dry and burning eyes. Up the lane, a cheerful, buoyant whistle was echoing. Shortly after, Pacifique Buote appeared in view.

chapter_title: Chapter XL A Book of Revelation
text: Without warning, Nell lost her bodily vigor. She had to grab a low willow branch to prevent herself from dropping down. Pacifique worked as a hired hand for Laurence Fletcher, whose residence was adjacent to the Carrows'. Mrs. Fletcher was the aunt of Hugh. Pacifique was sure to be aware if—if—Pacifique would be informed about whatever might be learned.

text: Pacifique was stepping along the red lane with a sturdy stride, whistling as he went. He failed to notice Nell. Three times she tried to call out to him in vain. He had nearly walked by when she finally managed to get her trembling lips to cry, “Pacifique!”

text: “Sure,” Pacifique said agreeably. “Las’ night I got de word dat my fader was seeck. Dat I couldn’t go den was because it was so stormy, so dis mornin’ I start vair early. For short cut, I’m goin’ troo de woods.”

chapter_title: Chapter XL A Book of Revelation
text: “Was there any news about how Hugh Carrow was doing this morning?” Her overwhelming desperation forced the question from Nell. Bearing even the direst outcome would prove easier than continuing to suffer through this dreadful uncertainty.

chapter_title: Chapter XL A Book of Revelation
text: “He is improving,” stated Pacifique. “He passed de turning point las’ night. De doctor claims he will recover fully in a short time now. It was a narrow escape, however! Dat boy, he almost killed himself at college. Well, I have to make haste. De old man, he will be eager to meet me.”

chapter_title: Chapter XL A Book of Revelation
text: Pacifique restarted his strolling and his whistling. Nell watched him walk away with eyes in which the night's tense agony was being expelled by delight. He was an exceedingly tall and thin, exceedingly tattered, exceedingly plain young man. Yet to her eyes he possessed the beauty of those bearing glad tidings upon the mountains. For the rest of her life, Nell would never behold Pacifique’s dark-skinned, circular, dark-eyed countenance without a affectionate memory of the instance in which he had bestowed upon her the oil of gladness instead of grief.

chapter_title: Chapter XL A Book of Revelation
text: It was long after Pacifique’s cheerful piping had dissolved into an echo of melody and subsequently into stillness far away beneath the maple trees of Linger Lane that Nell remained beneath the willows, savoring how intensely sweet life feels once a major terror has been lifted from it. The morning resembled a vessel brimming with fog and magic. In the nook close to her lay a lavish wonder of newly opened roses coated in crystal dew. The warbles and drips of music coming from the birds perched in the large tree over her appeared to be in complete harmony with how she felt. A phrase originating from a remarkably ancient, deeply accurate, incredibly marvelous Book rose to her lips,

chapter_title: Chapter XL A Book of Revelation
text: “Sorrow might last through the night, yet happiness arrives with the dawn.”

This gown requires some alterations from me, and once those are completed, my preparation for the event must begin. I am terribly grieved. My heart would delight in joining you.”

chapter_title: Chapter XLI Love Takes Up the Glass of Time
text: Nell watched him walk away with long strides, and released a sigh. Hugh was amiable—extremely amiable—much too amiable. Subsequent to his restoration to health, he had visited Grey Shutters frequently, and a portion of their former fellowship had been restored. However, it no longer contented Nell. When set against the rose of love, friendship's bloom seemed washed-out and lacking fragrance. Furthermore, Nell had once more started to question whether Hugh currently experienced any emotion for her beyond friendship. The brilliant assurance she felt on that enraptured morning had dimmed in the ordinary light of an ordinary day. A wretched dread tormented her that her error was impossible to correct. It was entirely possible that Rowena was the one Hugh actually loved. It might be that he was even betrothed to her. Nell attempted to banish every disturbing expectation from her soul, and adapt to a destiny in which labor and aspiration would have to substitute for love. As an instructor, she was capable of doing worthwhile, if not grand, work; while the favor her modest drawings were starting to receive in some editorial offices boded well for her developing writerly ambitions. Yet—yet—Nell lifted her green gown and let out another sigh.

chapter_title: Chapter XLI Love Takes Up the Glass of Time
text: Upon Hugh's arrival the following afternoon, Nell was expecting him, looking as fresh as dawn and as fair as a star, despite the previous night's festivities. She had put on a green dress—different from her wedding attire, but a former dress that Hugh had singled out as a favorite during a Wexcombe reception. This precise hue of green highlighted the deep tones of her hair, the star-like gray of her eyes, and her skin's delicate, iris-like complexion. Walking beside her on a shaded woodland trail, Hugh looked at her from the corner of his eye and felt she was more beautiful than ever before. Stealing occasional side glances at Hugh, Nell reflected on how significantly older he appeared after his sickness. He seemed to have relinquished his youth permanently.

chapter_title: Chapter XLI Love Takes Up the Glass of Time
text: The weather was splendid and the route was splendid. Nell felt a slight regret when they arrived at Dinah Wren’s garden and took a seat on the ancient bench. Yet that place possessed splendour as well—just as splendid as it was on the distant day of the Golden Picnic, when Isolde and Odette and Honora and she had discovered it. At that time, narcissus and violets made it lovely; currently, golden rod had lit its fairy torches in the corners and asters scattered blue spots across it. From the birch valley, the brook's call drifted up through the trees carrying every bit of its former fascination; the purr of the sea saturated the soft air; further out lay fields bordered by fences that multi-summer suns had bleached to a silvery gray, alongside sprawling hills draped in the shadows of autumn clouds; as the west wind blew, former dreams came back.

chapter_title: Chapter XLI Love Takes Up the Glass of Time
text: “It seems to me,” Nell uttered in a quiet voice, “that ‘the land where dreams come true’ lies within the blue haze over there, past that small valley.”

chapter_title: Chapter XLI Love Takes Up the Glass of Time
text: “Are there any dreams you have not fulfilled, Nell?” Hugh asked.

chapter_title: Chapter XLI Love Takes Up the Glass of Time
text: Nell’s heart began to throb furiously because of a particular quality in his voice—a quality that she had not detected since that wretched night in the orchard at Tabby’s Place. She replied, however, in an airy manner.

text: “Naturally. Everyone does. Having all our wishes realized would not be good for us. If there remained nothing for us to imagine, we might as well be dead. chapter_title: Chapter XLI Love Takes Up the Glass of Time
text: Nell wished to express herself, yet no words came to her. A surge of happiness washed over her like a wave. She felt nearly terrified by it.

text: “Nell, I posed a question to you more than two years back. Should I repeat that inquiry today, will your response be any different?”

text: “I believed Rowena Calder was the object of your affection,” Nell said to him, speaking with as much disapproval as though she had not provided him with complete cause to assume that Cyril Lisle had her own love.

chapter_title: Chapter XLI Love Takes Up the Glass of Time
text: Hugh uttered a youthful laugh.

chapter_title: Chapter XLI Love Takes Up the Glass of Time
text: “Rowena was betrothed to a person in her native town. This was known to me, and she was aware that I knew it. Upon his graduation, her brother informed me that his sister intended to come to Portmaris the following winter for music study, and he requested that I pay her some attention, since she was unacquainted with anyone and would feel quite lonely. Therefore, I obliged. Subsequently, I grew fond of Rowena on her own merits. She ranks among the finest girls I have ever encountered. I was mindful that campus rumors attributed a romantic involvement to us. It was of no concern to me. For a period back then, after you informed me that you could never care for me, Nell, nothing held much significance for me. There was no other person—for me, there could never be anyone but you. My love for you has endured from the moment you shattered your slate across my head at school.”

chapter_title: Chapter XLI Love Takes Up the Glass of Time
text: “I fail to understand how your love for me could persist while I behaved like such a silly girl,” Nell remarked.

chapter_title: Chapter XLI Love Takes Up the Glass of Time
text: “Indeed, I attempted to cease,” Hugh admitted openly, “not owing to a belief that you were what you term yourself, but since I was convinced my prospects vanished once Lisle arrived. Yet I was unable to—and it is impossible to express the impact it had on me over those two years when I thought you would wed him, and received weekly reports from various meddlers stating the public declaration of your betrothal was imminent. My belief persisted until a wonderful day while I was convalescing following the fever. A missive arrived for me from Cressy Lindsay—or more accurately, Cressy Hale—where she informed me that you and Cyril were actually not involved, and suggested I ‘try again.’ Truly, the physician was astonished by how quickly I got better following that.”

chapter_title: Chapter XLI Love Takes Up the Glass of Time
text: Nell giggled, and after that she shuddered.

chapter_title: Chapter XLI Love Takes Up the Glass of Time
text: “I will always remember that evening when I believed you were passing away, Hugh. Oh, I was aware—I was aware right then—and I believed the time had already run out.”

chapter_title: Chapter XLI Love Takes Up the Glass of Time
text: “However, it was not, my love. Ah, Nell, does this not compensate for all else? Let us make a vow to reserve this date forever to pure loveliness throughout our existence because of the present it has granted us.”

chapter_title: Chapter XLI Love Takes Up the Glass of Time
text: “It’s the anniversary of our joy,” Nell murmured. “This old garden belonging to Dinah Wren has always been beloved by me, and from now on it will be even more precious.”

chapter_title: Chapter XLI Love Takes Up the Glass of Time
text: “However, Nell, you must be prepared for a lengthy wait,” Hugh remarked mournfully. “Three years will pass before my studies in medicine are complete. Furthermore, even at that point, marble halls and diamond sunbursts will not be ours.”

chapter_title: Chapter XLI Love Takes Up the Glass of Time
text: A laugh came from Nell.

chapter_title: Chapter XLI Love Takes Up the Glass of Time
text: “Sunbursts and marble halls are not what I desire. My only wish is for you. As you can tell, I have just as little shame regarding this as Cressy. While marble halls and sunbursts might be perfectly fine, lacking them offers greater ‘scope for imagination’. Furthermore, the period of waiting is unimportant. Happy is what we will be, as we wait and work for one another—and dream. Oh, sweet dreams are what we will have now.”

chapter_title: Chapter XLI Love Takes Up the Glass of Time
text: Hugh pulled her near to his side and pressed his lips to hers. Afterwards, they strolled back to their house as one during the twilight, reigning as king and queen within love's matrimonial domain, treading meandering trails edged by the most fragrant blossoms to ever flower, and traversing enchanted fields swept by breezes of expectation and remembrance.
